chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who entered the land of war under a guarantee of safety, and then a different group attacked the people he had entered among. He said: 'It is upon the Muslim to protect himself and to fight according to the ruling of Allah and the ruling of His Messenger. As for fighting the disbelieents according to their ruling of injustice and their custom, that is not permissible for him.'

key_terms.حُكْمِ الْجَوْرِ: Ruling of injustice (custom of the enemy based on injustice)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between fighting according to God's law and fighting according to the enemy's custom in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the criteria for legitimate combat are refined by contrasting adherence to divine justice with imitation of pagan customs, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the moral integrity of the warrior. This highlights that the legitimacy of jihad depends not only on the enemy's status but on whether the Muslim fighter aligns his actions with the Sunnah of the Prophet rather than merely adopting the 'rules of war' of the disbelievers. It serves as a foundational principle for ensuring that military conduct remains a reflection of divine will rather than strategic expediency or cultural mimicry.
